title: Implement Dynamic Risk-Based Transaction Throttling
description: To comply with new anti-money laundering (AML) regulations, PayPalsphere must implement a dynamic transaction throttling mechanism. This feature will prevent users from performing rapid, successive transactions that might indicate suspicious activity. The system should identify high-velocity transaction patterns, place a temporary 'cooldown' on the user's account, and block further transactions until the cooldown period expires. This is a critical modification to the core transaction processing and risk assessment flow, requiring careful, incremental implementation across multiple microservices while respecting the existing CQRS and Event Sourcing architecture.

project_spec.name: PayPalsphere
project_spec.description:
PayPalsphere is a socially-driven fintech payment ecosystem where users can create circles (friends, family, communities or business cohorts), share payment timelines, split expenses in real time, and transparently track financial commitments together. Beyond the classic wallet, every transaction becomes a social post that can be tagged, commented on, privately reacted to, or publicly celebrated, turning payments into conversational events. When a member of a circle triggers a payment or a settlement request, the platform automatically orchestrates KYC verification, risk scoring, fraud screening, multi-currency conversion, and regulatory compliance—all surfaced through a collaborative, feed-based interface.

Built entirely with a component-based architecture, each bounded context (Accounts, KYC, Risk, Transactions, Compliance, Social Graph, Notification, and Settlement) is encapsulated as a discrete micro-frontend and micro-service pair. CQRS with Event Sourcing records every intent and state transition as immutable events, enabling fine-grained audit trails and historical replay for investigative or social storytelling purposes ("relive your group trip expenses"). Security-by-Design governs every component, weaving field-level encryption, role-based policies, and consent management into each workflow. Sagas coordinate long-running, multi-step social payments—such as collective fundraising or group-order settlement—while a dedicated Audit Trail service streams signed logs to cold storage for regulatory and community transparency. The result is a highly modular, socially interactive payment network that can evolve or be forked into new social sub-communities without cross-cutting concerns.
dependencies: React + Module Federation (micro-frontends for Social UI)
KafkaJS (event bus for CQRS / Saga coordination)
